title: Simplex-lift criterion for a right-anodyne decomposition inclusion
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small ordinary category, and $F:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/K}$ a functor, written $a\mapsto(\pi_a:K_a\to K)$; its arrows are simplicial maps commuting with the maps to $K$. Let $K_F$ be the decomposition simplicial set specified in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones]: an $n$-simplex has a cut $-1\leq i\leq n$, a lower simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K$ when $i\geq0$, an upper chain $a_{i+1}\to\cdots\to a_n$ when $i<n$, and lifts $\sigma_j:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K_{a_j}$ for $j>i$, with $\pi_{a_j}\sigma_j=\sigma$ and $F(a_j\to a_k)\sigma_j=\sigma_k$. The all-upper case is a simplex of $N(I)$ and the all-lower case is a simplex of $K$; operators restrict or repeat the two blocks and compose the arrows, retaining the pure simplex when a block disappears. For every simplex $z\in K_m$, define the ordinary category $I_z$ to have objects $(a,w)$ with $w\in(K_a)_m$ and $\pi_a(w)=z$, and arrows $(a,w)\to(b,w')$ the arrows $u:a\to b$ of $I$ with $F(u)(w)=w'$. Let $D_z\subseteq I_z$ be the full subcategory on those pairs for which $w$ is degenerate, meaning that $w$ is the pullback of a lower-dimensional simplex along a noninjective surjective monotone map. Suppose that $N(I_z)$ is weakly contractible for every nondegenerate simplex $z$ of $K$, and that $N(D_z)\hookrightarrow N(I_z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every degenerate simplex $z$ of $K$. Then the pure-upper inclusion $N(I)\hookrightarrow K_F$ is right anodyne. Neither $K$ nor any $K_a$ is required to be a quasicategory; $I$ need not be a poset or directed, and the maps $\pi_a$ need not be injective.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1 and Notation 4.2.3.7, Proposition 4.2.3.8, printed pp. 248-252. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: For a face-stable family $L_m\subseteq K_m$, let $L_F$ contain all pure-upper simplices and exactly those other simplices whose unique nondegenerate root in $K_F$ has lower block in $L$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] here for $K_F$, not merely for $K$. This is a simplicial subset: degeneracies preserve the nondegenerate root, and for a face the lower block of its nondegenerate root is an iterated face of the original lower block. Indeed, deleting lower vertices takes faces, deleting upper vertices composes arrows, and removing lower degeneracies can be performed by a monotone section of the corresponding surjection, hence by taking a face. A monotone surjection has such a section by choosing the least element of each nonempty fiber. Face stability therefore gives closure. To construct the filtration, well-order each set $K_m$ and order the disjoint union of ALL the $K_m$ first by dimension and then by these orders; include degenerate simplices as separate elements. Every proper face precedes its simplex. Initial segments are thus face-stable; at a successor we add just one simplex $\sigma\in K_m$. The associated $L_F$ start at $N(I)$, end at $K_F$, and commute with unions at limit ordinals because membership is decided by one nondegenerate root. This filtration is not indexed by nondegenerate simplices of $K$: a nondegenerate simplex of $K_a$ may have degenerate image in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, proof, first paragraph (PDF p. 270): the subsets L_F and reduction to adjoining one simplex; Notation 4.2.3.1

proof.text: For any successor $L'=L\cup\{\sigma\}$ with $\sigma\in K_m$, construct the characteristic map $c_\sigma:\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)\to L'_F$ directly. On a mixed simplex, a monotone map $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ and a chain $(a_0,w_0)\to\cdots\to(a_s,w_s)$ give lower block $\alpha^*\sigma$, upper chain $a_0\to\cdots\to a_s$, and lifts $\alpha^*w_j$; on pure factors use $\sigma:\Delta^m\to K$ and the forgetful nerve map to $N(I)$. These formulas commute with all operators. The boundary-join maps into $L_F$, since its lower block is a proper face of $\sigma$ or a degeneracy of one. To verify the resulting pushout, examine nondegenerate simplices. A mixed simplex of $K_F$ is nondegenerate exactly when its first lift is nondegenerate and all arrows in its upper chain are nonidentity: a degeneracy wholly in the lower block is precisely a degeneracy of the first lift (and hence of every subsequent lift), one wholly in the upper block repeats an identity arrow, and no degeneracy can cross the two blocks. Nondegenerate simplices of the characteristic join outside its boundary-join have full lower simplex $\mathrm{id}_{[m]}$; their upper chains retain every lift as data, so distinct such chains have distinct mixed images whenever their first lifts are nondegenerate. If $\sigma$ is nondegenerate, every lift of it is nondegenerate, since a simplicial map preserves degeneracies. The remaining pure lower simplex also maps to the new nondegenerate simplex $\sigma$. Thus these are exactly, and bijectively, the nondegenerate simplices of $L'_F$ outside $L_F$. Unique nondegenerate decomposition from Step 1 gives the same pushout degree by degree, including all degeneracies. Consequently this successor is a pushout of $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$. Apply [lem-coef-contractible-join-right-anodyne] with $A_0=\partial\Delta^m$, $A=\Delta^m$ and $B=N(I_\sigma)$; its weak-contractibility hypothesis is exactly the assumed nondegenerate-simplex condition.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, proof, nondegenerate case (PDF p. 270), using Lemma 4.2.3.6

proof.text: Now let the adjoined $\sigma\in K_m$ be degenerate. Use the characteristic map $c_\sigma$ explicitly defined in Step 2 and set $B=N(I_\sigma)$, $B_0=N(D_\sigma)$. A chain belongs to $B_0$ exactly when its first lift is degenerate: that condition is preserved by every $F(u)$, so then every object of the chain lies in the full subcategory $D_\sigma$. For such a chain, a degeneracy presentation of its first lift supplies a common lower-block degeneracy for every lift, and the resulting mixed simplex of $K_F$ has nondegenerate root with lower dimension less than $m$; it therefore lies in $L_F$. Also the pure lower simplex $\sigma$ has smaller-dimensional root and is old. Accordingly $c_\sigma$ maps the subobject $P=(\partial\Delta^m\star B)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^m\star B_0}(\Delta^m\star B_0)$ into $L_F$; the join convention includes the entire pure lower factor in $\Delta^m\star B_0$, even when $B_0$ is empty. A nondegenerate simplex outside $P$ must be mixed, with full lower $\mathrm{id}_{[m]}$ and a nonidentity upper chain whose first lift is nondegenerate. By the criterion in Step 2 its image is nondegenerate with lower block $\sigma$, and its complete list of lifts and arrows is recovered from that image. Conversely every new nondegenerate simplex of $L'_F$ has these data, so these images are bijectively all the new nondegenerate simplices. Unique decomposition from Step 1 then proves the pushout square with top map $P\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star B$ degree by degree. The inclusion $B_0\hookrightarrow B$ is degreewise injective (chains in a full subcategory remain distinct) and a weak homotopy equivalence by the assumed degenerate-simplex condition. Apply [lem-coef-join-pushout-right-anodyne] with $A_0=\partial\Delta^m$, $A=\Delta^m$, $B_0=N(D_\sigma)$ and $B=N(I_\sigma)$ to conclude that the attaching map is right anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, proof, degenerate case (PDF p. 270), using Lemma 4.2.3.5

proof.text: The disjoint union $\coprod_{m\geq0}K_m$ is small, so the dimension-first well-order of ALL simplices in Step 1 has small ordinal type. Each successor inclusion of the continuous filtration is the pushout of a right-anodyne map proved in Step 2 or Step 3. At each limit ordinal its simplicial subset is the degreewise union of the earlier subsets, as established in Step 1. The pushout and transfinite-composition clauses in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] therefore show that the composite $N(I)=L_{F,\varnothing}\hookrightarrow L_{F,K}=K_F$ is right anodyne.
